title: Worksheet 2: RAM vs. Storage (V2.0)
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: Computers use two very different kinds of memory: RAM and storage, and people often confuse the two. RAM, which stands for Random Access Memory, is a type of short-term memory that a computer uses to hold information it is actively working on right now, such as an open program or a document you are currently editing. RAM is extremely fast, but it is also "volatile," meaning that everything stored in RAM disappears the moment the computer loses power or shuts down. Storage, such as a hard drive or solid-state drive (SSD), is different: it holds information permanently, even after the computer is turned off, which is why your files, photos, and installed programs are still there the next time you turn the computer on. Storage is generally much slower than RAM, but it can hold far more information over a long period of time. A helpful comparison is that RAM is like a person's short-term memory of what they're doing right now, while storage is like a filing cabinet that keeps records long-term.

questions.text: According to the paragraph, what does RAM stand for?
According to the paragraph, what does "volatile" mean for RAM?
questions.correct: Everything stored in it disappears when the computer loses power
distractors: It heats up quickly during use
It can hold far more data than storage

questions.text: According to the paragraph, which is generally faster?
According to the paragraph, RAM and storage are compared to:
questions.correct: Short-term memory and a filing cabinet

questions.text: A student's computer loses power while they are typing an unsaved essay. Based on the paragraph, why is the work gone?
questions.correct: It was held in RAM, which is erased when power is lost
distractors: Storage deletes files when a computer restarts
The essay was too large for the hard drive
RAM only holds numbers, not text
